summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, chronic pain, and recent steroid use was admitted with acute left lower quadrant abdominal pain and watery diarrhea following a meal with a friend who also became ill. Initial concern for a Crohn’s flare was ruled out by normal inflammatory markers and stable findings on recent imaging. Stool studies showed no bacterial, parasitic, or C. difficile infection, supporting a diagnosis of viral gastroenteritis. The patient was managed supportively with IV then oral pain control. Azathioprine was held due to mild thrombocytopenia. Pain Management recommended starting tizanidine and Lyrica for chronic pain. The patient improved clinically and was discharged home on prednisone, pantoprazole, loperamide as needed, and new pain medications, with instructions to follow up with gastroenterology and pain specialists.
problems: Intestinal infection due to other organism, not elsewhere classified
